ProgressPage.title: Your progress
ProgressPage.empty: Nothing to show yet. Take a quiz or review some cards and your progress will appear here.
ProgressPage.intro: What your quiz answers and card reviews say about how well you know each topic. These are estimates: the more you answer, the more they mean.
ProgressPage.bandsHint: Only questions written with the experimental level labels are split this way.
ProgressPage.howBody: Right answers count for more when they are recent (they fade over about 45 days) and when they are hard to get by luck: an open answer counts for more than a true/false one. One answer never reads as 100%, and a number is shown only once there is enough evidence behind it. Blank answers and questions you flagged as faulty are ignored, and a question you answered several times counts once, with your latest answer. Card memory is the chance you still remember the cards you have reviewed, worked out from their review schedule.

WelcomePage.note1: By default everything stays on your device — conversion, search, and local (Ollama) chat never send data anywhere. If you pick a cloud provider (e.g. Deepseek, Gemini), that chat's content goes to that provider; importing a link or YouTube video sends a request to that address.

SettingsPage.allowConcurrentGenerationHint: Off by default — quiz/card/report/map/slide generation waits for an existing generation of the same type to finish before starting a new one, so they don't all slow each other down on weaker hardware. Turn this on if your hardware can handle it.
SettingsPage.quizLevelLabels: Label quiz questions by cognitive level (experimental)
SettingsPage.quizLevelLabelsHint: Off by default. Asks the model to write each question for a cognitive level (recall, understanding, application, higher) so progress can be reported per level. On a small local model (8B) the fine labels are unreliable: an independent check agreed with them only about half the time, and it cannot tell "recall" from "understanding" consistently. The coarse split (remember/explain versus apply/analyse) held up better, about 80%. Turn it on with a stronger model; with a small one, treat the labels as a rough hint.

SettingsPage.showWelcomeScreenHint: Turning this off opens the app straight into the vault picker.

LibrarySettingsPage.title: Library
LibrarySettingsPage.importObsidianDescription: Copies an Obsidian vault one-way (the source is never written to). Wikilinks are converted to relative markdown links, attachments are copied, and notes missing frontmatter fields get a default value plus a review badge.
LibrarySettingsPage.importLinksDescription: Paste PDF and web page links — they're downloaded in sequence and added to the library. Links already imported successfully are skipped on a re-run.
LibrarySettingsPage.keepOriginals: Keep the original files of converted documents ({path})
LibrarySettingsPage.allowedLanguagesHint: The first language is the vault's primary/fallback language: with "Answer in the question's language" it's used when the last message's language can't be determined; with "Always answer in the primary language" it's always used. Additional languages (e.g. for a language-learning vault) may appear in the response and aren't flagged as corruption by the leak detector.
LibrarySettingsPage.responseLanguageFixed: Always answer in the primary language
LibrarySettingsPage.responseLanguageHint: "Answer in the question's language" detects the last user message's own language (an English question gets an English answer, a Turkish one gets Turkish). "Always answer in the primary language" is the original behavior — for vaults like language-learning ones where the target language must stay fixed.
LibrarySettingsPage.hiddenFolders: Folders hidden in the chat screen
LibrarySettingsPage.hiddenFoldersHint: These root folders never appear in the chat's source tree and are never offered as a source to any generation (chat, quiz, report, ...). The Library Tree (below) is unaffected.
LibrarySettingsPage.flattenFolders: Folders flattened in the chat screen
LibrarySettingsPage.flattenFoldersHint: These root folders themselves are hidden; the folders beneath them are shown directly at the tree's root instead. Paths are unchanged — only the tree's appearance is simplified.
LibrarySettingsPage.libraryTreeDescription: Upload, rename, or delete documents. The chat screen's own source tree (Faz 9) uses a separate, read-only copy of this for scope selection instead.

ProvidersSettingsPage.title: Model Providers
ProvidersSettingsPage.intro: Manage your local servers (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, ...) and optional cloud providers (DeepSeek, OpenAI, ...). Keys stay on the server in {path} and are never sent to the browser.
ProvidersSettingsPage.secretsPlaintextWarning: API keys are stored unencrypted on this computer. Anyone who can read your user files can read them.
ProvidersSettingsPage.secretsPlaintextWarningLinux: API keys are stored unencrypted on this computer because no system keyring was found. Install and enable GNOME Keyring or KWallet (a Secret Service provider), then restart the app to encrypt them.
ProvidersSettingsPage.secretsResetManual: To recover manually: quit the app, rename {path} to something like secrets.json.old (keep it as a backup) and remove the stored encryption key — on Windows rename secrets.key in the same folder; on macOS delete the "secrets-key" item of "app.vaultchat.desktop" in Keychain Access; on Linux delete it in Passwords and Keys / KWallet. Then start the app and enter your API keys again.
ProvidersSettingsPage.secretsResetConfirmDescription: Your saved API keys will be set aside and you will have to enter them again. Nothing is deleted: the old file is kept as a backup next to the original ({path}, renamed to secrets.json.locked-<date and time>). The app will restart.

ProvidersSettingsPage.secretsLockedError: Saved API keys can't be unlocked — the system keychain refused access or is locked. Your keys were not replaced; unlock the keychain and restart the app.
